F1:
A ProximityPrompt only works when its parent is a BasePart, an Attachment, or a Model that has a PrimaryPart set, and that parent must be in Workspace. A Folder is not a valid parent, so the prompt never appears. A Model without a PrimaryPart also fails, which is why moving it into another Model didn't help.
Fix: parent the prompt to an Attachment placed at the counter or handle, or to a BasePart, or set the Model's PrimaryPart.
The 'only from some angles' problem comes from RequiresLineOfSight, which defaults to true. Roblox checks for a clear line from the camera to the prompt's parent, so other parts of the stand block it from some sides. Put the prompt on an Attachment on the visible front face, or set RequiresLineOfSight = false. Also check MaxActivationDistance (default 10 studs), Enabled, and that the parent isn't buried inside a large part.
Sources: ProximityPrompt - Engine Reference Card; Clickable and Interactive Parts.
F2:
1) Ownership (nothing plays live): the animation asset must be owned by the same creator as the experience. For a group game, publish or re-upload the animation under the group (set Creator to the group), or grant the experience permission on the asset in Creator Dashboard. A Studio solo test can load your personal animations; live servers can't. To diagnose, check the Output for a load or permission error, or see whether track.Length stays 0.
2) Half-blended with walking: this is a priority problem. A track left at Core (or Idle/Movement) blends with the default walk. Set the animation's Priority to Action (or Action2-4) in the editor or with track.Priority = Enum.AnimationPriority.Action. Rank: Core < Idle < Movement < Action < Action2-4. Don't compare by .Value, because Core = 1000.
3) Humanoid:LoadAnimation is deprecated. Use humanoid:FindFirstChildOfClass('Animator'):LoadAnimation(anim). The Animator should be created by the server (the default character already has one). Loading it from the client's own character is fine and replicates.
4) Load each track once and cache it. Every LoadAnimation call makes a new track, and there is a limit of about 256 tracks.
Sources: Publishing Animations; Playback, Priorities and Blending; Animator Deep Dive.
F3:
1) LayoutOrder is only used when the UIListLayout's SortOrder = Enum.SortOrder.LayoutOrder. Your layout is set to SortOrder = Name, so it sorts the children alphabetically by Instance.Name and ignores LayoutOrder. Fix: layout.SortOrder = Enum.SortOrder.LayoutOrder. Then 10, 50, 200, 1000 sort ascending, smallest first. Gapped values like these make it easy to insert items later.
2) Equal LayoutOrder: ties have no stable, guaranteed order. Siblings with the same LayoutOrder can come out in a different order between sessions or after re-parenting or renaming, so they appear to 'swap'. Give every item a unique LayoutOrder, for example price*10 + index, or break ties by encoding a second key.
Also: SortOrder = Name re-sorts when items are renamed. Only direct children with a GuiObject are laid out.
Source: UI Layout Objects - Lists, Grids and Pages.
F4:
```lua
-- ServerScriptService, the ONLY ProcessReceipt in the game
local MPS = game:GetService("MarketplaceService")
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local Data = require(script.Parent.PlayerData) -- session-locked profile store
local PRODUCTS = { [123456] = function(profile) profile.Coins += 100 end }

MPS.ProcessReceipt = function(info)
  local player = Players:GetPlayerByUserId(info.PlayerId)
  if not player then return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet end
  local profile = Data.get(player)
  local grant = PRODUCTS[info.ProductId]
  if not profile or not grant then return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet end
  if profile.Receipts[info.PurchaseId] then return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.PurchaseGranted end
  grant(profile)
  profile.Receipts[info.PurchaseId] = os.time()
  local ok = Data.saveNow(player) -- pcall'd save of the same document
  if not ok then return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet end
  return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.PurchaseGranted
end
```
Rules:
- Have exactly one ProcessReceipt. A second assignment silently replaces the first.
- Return PurchaseGranted only after the grant is durably saved. On any failure, or if the player is absent, return NotProcessedYet; Roblox retries on their next join or purchase.
- Make it idempotent: store processed PurchaseIds in the same profile and the same save as the coins (not in a separate store).
- Never grant from PromptProductPurchaseFinished or from client remotes.
- Don't error or yield indefinitely inside the callback, and trim old receipt ids.
Source: Developer Products and ProcessReceipt.
F5:
```lua
-- StarterPlayerScripts/Sprint (LocalScript)
local CAS = game:GetService("ContextActionService")
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local player = Players.LocalPlayer
local WALK, RUN = 16, 24

local function getHum()
  local c = player.Character
  return c and c:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
end

local function onSprint(_, state, _)
  local hum = getHum()
  if not hum then return Enum.ContextActionResult.Pass end
  if state == Enum.UserInputState.Begin then
    hum.WalkSpeed = RUN
  elseif state == Enum.UserInputState.End or state == Enum.UserInputState.Cancel then
    hum.WalkSpeed = WALK
  end
  return Enum.ContextActionResult.Sink
end

CAS:BindAction("Sprint", onSprint, true, Enum.KeyCode.LeftShift, Enum.KeyCode.ButtonL3)
CAS:SetTitle("Sprint", "Run")
CAS:SetPosition("Sprint", UDim2.new(1, -170, 1, -90))
player.CharacterAdded:Connect(function() local h = getHum() if h then h.WalkSpeed = WALK end end)
```
Rules:
- CAS runs client-side only. createTouchButton = true makes the button, which appears only on touch devices (GetButton returns nil elsewhere).
- Handle Begin, End and Cancel. Cancel fires when the binding is replaced or unbound, so reset the speed there.
- Return Sink to consume the input or Pass to let it through.
- Name actions by intent, and UnbindAction when the context ends.
- WalkSpeed set on the client replicates (the client owns its character), so the server should sanity-check speed.
- CAS BindAction is slated for deprecation in favor of the Input Action System.
F6:
```lua
-- Server Script. Frame is Anchored; Door is unanchored (not welded to the frame).
local hinge = workspace.DoorModel.HingeConstraint -- Attachment0 on Frame, Attachment1 on Door
hinge.ActuatorType = Enum.ActuatorType.Servo
hinge.AngularSpeed = math.rad(90) -- radians/sec: about 1 s to swing
hinge.ServoMaxTorque = 1e6 -- enough to beat door mass and friction
hinge.LimitsEnabled = true
hinge.LowerAngle, hinge.UpperAngle = 0, 90 -- degrees
workspace.DoorModel.Door:SetNetworkOwner(nil) -- server-owned, so exploiters can't fling it

local open = false
local function setOpen(v)
  open = v
  hinge.TargetAngle = v and 90 or 0 -- degrees
end
workspace.DoorModel.Door.ProximityPrompt.Triggered:Connect(function() setOpen(not open) end)
```
Properties that matter:
- ActuatorType Servo (Motor just spins), TargetAngle in degrees, AngularSpeed (rad/s), ServoMaxTorque (too low means the door sags or stalls).
- LimitsEnabled with LowerAngle and UpperAngle as hard stops.
- Both attachments' primary axis (X) must point along the hinge line (vertical): rotate the attachments so their axes align.
- Only the frame is anchored. The door must be unanchored and not welded to the frame, and anything welded to the door moves with it.
- Keep the door server-owned (SetNetworkOwner(nil)). A client-owned door can be desynced.
Source: Physics Assemblies and Constraints; Network Ownership.
F7:
Architecture:
1) Admin UI or chat command -> RemoteEvent -> server. The server verifies the sender with a server-side allowlist (UserId or group rank) and never trusts the client. Rate-limit the command.
2) Filter the text with TextService:FilterStringAsync(text, userId), then GetNonChatStringForBroadcastAsync().
3) In task.spawn, call pcall(MessagingService.PublishAsync, MessagingService, "Announce", {text=..., id=..., t=os.time()}). Don't block the remote handler.
4) Every server calls MessagingService:SubscribeAsync("Announce", function(msg) ... end) once at startup, inside pcall with retry. It then does RemoteEvent:FireAllClients(msg.Data) and the clients show the banner. Dedupe by id and drop stale messages using msg.Sent.
Limits (Roblox docs, subject to change):
- Payload is 1 kB max.
- Sends per server: 600 + 240 x players per minute.
- Receives per topic: 40 + 80 x servers per minute. Receives for the whole experience: 400 + 200 x servers per minute.
- Subscriptions per server: 20 + 8 x players. Subscribe requests: 240/min per server.
- Delivery is best effort, typically 1-2 s, and not guaranteed or ordered. For a must-see message, also store it, e.g. in a MemoryStore or DataStore key that new servers read.
- Publish rarely; one topic suits low-frequency announcements. Studio behavior differs; test in live servers.
- Open Cloud publishMessage (an external admin panel) shares the same limits.
Source: MessagingService - Engine Reference Card; Cross-Server Messaging.
F8:
Split:
- Client does feel only: plays the swing animation, sound and VFX immediately on Tool.Activated. It fires a RemoteEvent saying 'swing' and nothing else: no target, no damage.
- Server is the authority:
  - Rate-limit the remote and enforce the swing cooldown, with about 50-80 ms tolerance for latency.
  - Check the player is alive and the tool is equipped.
  - After the windup, re-check state and do its own hit query, e.g. workspace:GetPartBoundsInBox in front of the HumanoidRootPart or a short raycast.
  - Dedupe hits per model and check distance and line of sight.
  - Apply Humanoid:TakeDamage (this respects ForceFields).
- Never take damage or targets from client args, and don't rely on the client's Touched. The client may optionally send a hit hint that the server validates by distance.
Equip problem: Tool.RequiresHandle defaults to true and needs a BasePart child named exactly 'Handle'. With only 'Blade', the tool won't equip or Equipped won't fire. Rename the MeshPart to 'Handle' and adjust GripPos/Grip. Alternatively, add a small Handle part welded to Blade, or set RequiresHandle = false and attach it yourself. Make sure Handle is unanchored and CanCollide is usually false. Also check ManualActivationOnly is false, or Activated won't fire from clicks.
Sources: Tools and Inventory Systems; Melee Combat System End to End.
F9:
UnreliableRemoteEvent fits high-frequency, transient, superseded-by-the-next-update data, like your aim direction: losing one packet doesn't matter because the next one replaces it. It has its own pool, so it doesn't clog the reliable remotes used for hits and purchases.
Constraints:
- Delivery is best effort and unordered: messages can be dropped or arrive out of order. It doesn't yield, and there are no RemoteFunction-style returns.
- Payloads over about 1,000 bytes are dropped silently. Send a few numbers, not tables of instances; e.g. pack yaw/pitch, or quantize into a buffer.
- Rate is roughly 500 calls/s per client, shared across remotes of that type, and the excess is dropped.
- Never use it for state changes or one-off events (start/stop, damage, purchases). A lost 'stop' sticks. Use RemoteEvent for those.
Also:
- Cut the rate to 10-20 Hz and interpolate on receivers.
- Send only when the value changed beyond a threshold.
- On the server, validate and rate-limit the input, then relay server-built values. FireAllClients only to players who need it (or nearby ones), not raw client args.
Source: RemoteEvents, RemoteFunctions and Unreliable Remotes; Network Performance.
F10:
1) Nil index: with StreamingEnabled, parts far away (or not yet arrived) don't exist on the client, so workspace.Map.Castle.Gate can be nil.
- Use WaitForChild down the chain, with timeouts: local gate = workspace:WaitForChild('Map'):WaitForChild('Castle', 10) and so on, then handle nil.
- Or tag the gate and use CollectionService:GetInstanceAddedSignal plus GetTagged, so it also handles stream-out and stream-in.
- Set the Castle model's ModelStreamingMode = Atomic so it arrives whole. Use Persistent only for the few models the client must always have.
- Code must also tolerate the gate streaming out again.
2) Void on teleport: the destination hasn't streamed in yet, so the player falls through. On the server, before moving them, call pcall(player.RequestStreamAroundAsync, player, targetPos, 5). Then check the player and character still exist and do character:PivotTo(CFrame.new(targetPos)).
- Optionally anchor the HumanoidRootPart briefly, or keep a Persistent landing platform.
- Defaults: StreamingMinRadius 64, StreamingTargetRadius 1024. Prefer StreamOutBehavior Opportunistic and ModelStreamingBehavior Improved.
- Don't disable streaming to hide the bug.
Source: Instance Streaming.
F11:
Luau's New Type Solver (a rewrite of type inference) reached general release in November 2025. Notes flag the exact date as partly unverified.
What changed:
- It became the default for non-strict scripts. Strict-mode (--!strict) projects were not migrated automatically.
- The Studio Beta Features toggle was removed (on 7 Jan 2026). Control is now a per-place setting.
- The new solver gives more accurate inference and enables new features: user-defined type functions, read/write property modifiers, and better keyof/index and refinements. It also reports new or different errors.
How to turn it on for a --!strict project:
- In Studio, select Workspace and set the UseNewLuauTypeSolver property (RolloutState) to Enabled. Default follows Roblox's rollout and Disabled opts out.
- Keep --!strict at the top of files. Workspace.LuauTypeCheckMode sets the mode for files without a directive.
- Expect a batch of new errors on a large strict codebase. Fix them on a branch, and make sure the whole team uses the same solver setting (same for external tooling like luau-lsp, which has its own new-solver flag).
Source: Luau Type System and Strict Mode; Engine and API Changes 2025-2026.
F12:
The Input Action System (IAS) is Roblox's newer, instance-based input-mapping system that supersedes ContextActionService. You declare actions and their bindings as instances instead of code.
Instances:
- InputContext: a group of actions, with Enabled, Priority and Sink. A higher-Priority context with Sink consumes its bound inputs from lower contexts.
- InputAction (child of a context): Type is Bool, Direction1D/2D/3D or ViewportPosition. Events are Pressed and Released (Bool only) and StateChanged; there's also GetState() and Fire().
- InputBinding (child of an action): KeyCode (or composite Up/Down/Left/Right keys, modifiers), and UIButton, which points at a GuiButton that drives the action on touch.
Jump example: put the instances in StarterGui (or under the PlayerGui), then:
```lua
local ctx = Instance.new("InputContext")
ctx.Parent = script
local jump = Instance.new("InputAction")
jump.Name = "Jump"
jump.Type = Enum.InputActionType.Bool
jump.Parent = ctx
local kb = Instance.new("InputBinding")
kb.KeyCode = Enum.KeyCode.Space
kb.Parent = jump
local btn = Instance.new("InputBinding")
btn.UIButton = script.Parent.JumpGui.JumpButton
btn.Parent = jump
jump.Pressed:Connect(function()
  local h = game.Players.LocalPlayer.Character and game.Players.LocalPlayer.Character:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
  if h then h.Jump = true end
end)
```
Notes:
- You can add a gamepad binding, e.g. ButtonA.
- Default player scripts move to IAS via Workspace.PlayerScriptsUseInputActionSystem (opt-in 2026, default planned early 2027).
- For analog actions, poll GetState(), because StateChanged won't fire while held steady.
Source: Input - UserInputService and ContextActionService; Server Authority and Input Migration 2026.
